fixes.explanation: SYNAGOGUE, friend? Straight for the holy building, no hesitation. I love that confidence! But Paul says this brother is praised by all the churches "…for his work in the gospel." (2 Corinthians 8:18) It's not a building. The good news itself is what he works on.

Paying his own way, baker? Look at you, spreadsheet open, balancing the travel budget! Paul never says who covers the trip. He says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) The proof is that he believes in the Corinthians.

Leaving home to travel does sound earnest, friend. Bags packed, door locked, the whole production! But that's not where Paul points. He says this brother's earnestness shows "…now even more so by his great confidence in you." (2 Corinthians 8:22) The proof is that he believes in the Corinthians.

Respect for Paul's authority? Friend, Paul is not fishing for a standing ovation here! He asks them to "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Love is on that list. Authority never shows up.

Courage under trial? Baker, you just made this sound like a movie trailer, deep voice and all! But Paul's ask is smaller and warmer: "…show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you." (2 Corinthians 8:24) Courage isn't named. Love is.

Checking on the teaching, friend? Sounds like somebody's holding a clipboard and squinting! But Paul sends the brothers "…in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said." (2 Corinthians 9:3) Nothing here about inspecting teaching. It's about the Corinthians being ready to give.
